<span id="paper-agent-research-agentheal-7e583bfa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0888c0bac73ed362">Why is finding a similarly titled page after hitting a login wall not necessarily successful AgentHeal recovery?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentheal">AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It may be another work, an unverifiable look-alike, or an older version. AgentHeal preserves the original objective: prefer an exact-version copy when available; disclose differences when only other versions remain; otherwise abstain and diagnose the barrier, asking the user for help when necessary. Topic similarity is not equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a requested metric from paper v2 cannot silently be replaced by v1. Use an institutional v2 copy if one exists; if only v1 remains, explicitly disclose the version difference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.39234-agentheal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0888c0bac73ed362">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentheal" data-paper-title="AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-830f20199202674b">Why must AgentHeal&#x27;s exact-copy and alternative-version source conditions remain different?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentheal">AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equation 1 requires the attributed source set to intersect available exact copies. When only other versions remain, the nonempty source set must lie entirely within those versions and declare other. Any prohibited action multiplies final success by zero. Strengthening the first branch to copies only, or relaxing the second to one version somewhere, changes the paper.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: with only v1 reachable, mixing v1 and a decoy fails even with an other declaration. When v2 is available, Equation 1 itself only checks that v2 is among the sources; it does not prove answer semantics are correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.39234-agentheal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-830f20199202674b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentheal" data-paper-title="AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b970fa978c2c178">AgentPerturb requires solvability after perturbation, whereas AgentHeal includes unrecoverable tasks. Is that contradictory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentheal">AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They target different behaviors. AgentPerturb compares paired robustness under the same objective and must not count destroyed solvability as capability loss. AgentHeal explicitly labels unrecoverable regimes to assess honest abstention, accurate diagnosis, and policy compliance rather than demand nonexistent answers. Recoverable and unrecoverable cases need separate reporting, not one undifferentiated answer-accuracy score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: deleting the only evidence while still requiring the original number is an unfair perturbation. Labeling that condition unsolvable and testing refusal to fabricate instead measures recovery reliability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 本地结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.39234-agentheal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b970fa978c2c178">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentheal" data-paper-title="AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2af7339ec7b269ff">The local diagnostic knows work, version, and reachable resources. Does it reveal the recovery path to an agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentheal">AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Those are independent evaluator annotations. The module calls no actor and must not supply them as actor observations. Source attribution and per-action policy judgments also come from external evaluators rather than local string rules. TS=0.5 across four synthetic truth-table cases verifies the decision contract, not agent capability. Real browser evaluation still needs separation of actor, gold, and judge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: directly providing copy_id to a model before scoring recovery leaks the path. An independent evaluator should inspect visits and attributed sources only after the model submits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与实现边界, 本地结果与负控, 代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.39234-agentheal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2af7339ec7b269ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:physical-engineering-exam" data-paper-title="PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-physical-engineering-exam-2277e47a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-98b62ddbf22d1aa8">Why does PLE require auditable engineering artifacts rather than only written answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aphysical-engineering-exam">PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long engineering tasks have multimodal inputs, constraints, and deliverable files. Experts or independent graders check whether actual outputs meet requirements. Fluent descriptions do not establish completed designs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A written explanation does not prove the corresponding engineering file exists or passes constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30537v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.30537-physical-engineering-exam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98b62ddbf22d1aa8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:physical-engineering-exam" data-paper-title="PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-481c8954021f31c4">Why use hard gate G to cut off objective credit instead of letting high objective values offset failed hard constraints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aphysical-engineering-exam">PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Engineering artifacts may optimize a target while violating requirements. All hard constraints must pass for the gated reward. Constraint ratios retain component information, and missing tasks score zero in the full denominator. Local aggregation consumes external grades, not independent physical or regulatory judgments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lightweight design that fails a load-bearing constraint cannot compensate with weight savings. Missing artifacts cannot be dropped from the average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30537v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.30537-physical-engineering-exam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-481c8954021f31c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:physical-engineering-exam" data-paper-title="PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c6c2ac1e4e4e940d">How does PLE&#x27;s hard-gated constraint score differ from scoring continuously by objective value alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aphysical-engineering-exam">PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>When any hard constraint fails, G=0 and objective optimization earns nothing; higher objective values cannot offset the violation. Expert rubrics and special site/MEP graders have separate rules, so one formula does not cover every task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>High efficiency cannot earn the 0.6GO′ term after any hard-constraint failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30537v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.30537-physical-engineering-exam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c6c2ac1e4e4e940d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:physical-engineering-exam" data-paper-title="PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-721a9cf4dbf5ae04">Why retain the complete task denominator and missing items in PLE aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aphysical-engineering-exam">PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Average each run over all tasks with missing scores at zero, then average three run means. Conditioning on successful submissions inflates results. Local scoring accepts external grades and artifact bytes, not independent certification of physical or regulatory correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only 10 of 85 tasks are complete, their average is not the full benchmark mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 离线验收接口. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30537v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.30537-physical-engineering-exam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-721a9cf4dbf5ae04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scope-replay" data-paper-title="SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-scope-replay-4a09ab7b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-27c3a63c95f1b011">Why does SCOPE save stateful API tapes from successful executions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascope-replay">SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rerunning all earlier scenarios after a program edit is expensive. A full tape records requests, public state before and after, and results or exceptions, enabling same-instance replay and surfacing differences for native diagnosis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A complete tape can screen an old successful case without immediately restarting the robot environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.23128-scope-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27c3a63c95f1b011">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scope-replay" data-paper-title="SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9bb2e7154e6a7783">Why doesn&#x27;t successful API tape replay prove program equivalence for every input or serve as a candidate acceptance gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascope-replay">SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay checks recorded cases with given state, responses, and exceptions, leaving unseen inputs unknown. It selects divergences worth diagnosing natively rather than requiring rollback of a successful candidate. Only native-environment success updates the accepted program; replay divergence is not environment failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changed return ordering on an old tape can prompt targeted retesting. A candidate that completed the native task is not rejected solely because an old tape is incompatible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.23128-scope-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9bb2e7154e6a7783">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scope-replay" data-paper-title="SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-47affe69bc9f6270">Are SCOPE replay divergence and failure in the actual environment the same conclusion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascope-replay">SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Divergence means the candidate differs from or cannot use a recorded witness and informs further search. Native failure requires real execution. Unknown is not failure, and replay cannot establish equivalence over all inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An extra API query can diverge from the tape without showing that the actual task fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.23128-scope-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47affe69bc9f6270">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scope-replay" data-paper-title="SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e999aba71132c35">Is matching only API names and return values enough for stateful SCOPE replay?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascope-replay">SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Also match requests and prior state, restore subsequent mutations, exceptions, and aliases, consume the complete tape, and make no extra external calls. Native success updates the accepted program; do not turn replay into acceptance or rollback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If two objects share one list, replaying them as independent copies changes later behavior even when the immediate result matches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.23128-scope-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e999aba71132c35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tool-bottleneck-bench" data-paper-title="ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-tool-bottleneck-bench-4ca26883" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2dd236615f6ba3b">Why does ToolBottleneckBench control tool catalogs, menus, workflows, and return encoding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atool-bottleneck-bench">ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Osaka</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool-agent failure may reflect interface and budget interactions rather than only model capability. Hold task facts and decisions fixed and manipulate R/V/W/D separately to identify pressure associated with outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A longer visible menu can raise selection costs for the same model without proving weaker reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21098">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21098-tool-bottleneck-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2dd236615f6ba3b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tool-bottleneck-bench" data-paper-title="ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c5fe57bc8a85b2fa">Why isn&#x27;t recording the first unmet obligation a completed causal attribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atool-bottleneck-bench">ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Osaka</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Obligation ordering provides a consistent label, but later failures can coexist. Hold task facts fixed and manipulate catalog, menu, workflow, and return state to study pressure. Truth-assisted routed menus are diagnostic, not oracle-free deployment ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failure to retrieve a tool is labeled first, but argument logic may also be wrong. Fixing retrieval may expose it; label order is not causal proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21098">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21098-tool-bottleneck-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c5fe57bc8a85b2fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tool-bottleneck-bench" data-paper-title="ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-868224bb54ceef90">How does a truth-assisted routed menu differ from an oracle-free production router?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atool-bottleneck-bench">ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Osaka</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Truth-assisted narrowing is a controlled condition. It localizes bottlenecks but does not show that a live system can autonomously find the same menu.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Showing only the already-known correct tool is different from retrieving it from a large catalog at deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21098">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21098-tool-bottleneck-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-868224bb54ceef90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tool-bottleneck-bench" data-paper-title="ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d4a1b13e4351da91">Can missing retrievals and infrastructure failures be dropped from the catalog-pressure ITT denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atool-bottleneck-bench">ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Osaka</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep them in the planned denominator; conditioning on available requests inflates selection rates. Distinguish first unmet obligation from separately logged termination reasons. Neither automatically establishes causation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only 80 of 100 planned requests obtain a menu, still report outcomes over all 100.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21098">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21098-tool-bottleneck-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d4a1b13e4351da91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:shortcut-sensitivity" data-paper-title="Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-shortcut-sensitivity-1f4bb949" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-53510aaefacc8ed3">Why does Shortcut Sensitivity first inspect construction cues in evaluation inputs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ashortcut-sensitivity">Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kontext</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool names, lengths, source markers, and repeated interactions can predict labels without genuine risk judgment. Audit label predictability, guard association, and construct-preserving paired interventions separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a tool name occurs in every unsafe case, a model may score well using that cue alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22243-shortcut-sensitivity/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53510aaefacc8ed3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:shortcut-sensitivity" data-paper-title="Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb9c6ae3c3a0bb7e">Why doesn&#x27;t tool-name predictability prove a guard uses the shortcut?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ashortcut-sensitivity">Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kontext</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Label predictability shows a construction cue. Guard association is a second check. Changing only the cue under matched conditions gives stronger behavioral evidence. Control random inconsistency and placebos; association, unsigned flips, and signed effects are distinct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A name lookup can score well when dangerous samples share a tool name. To test guard reliance, rename it without changing behavior and compare decisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22243-shortcut-sensitivity/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb9c6ae3c3a0bb7e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:shortcut-sensitivity" data-paper-title="Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac8c0a7f5918e56a">Do label predictability, guard-decision association, and paired intervention effects imply each other?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ashortcut-sensitivity">Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kontext</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The first two motivate testing. Interventions must change only the cue while preserving risk and controlling random guard behavior and format placebos. Correlation is insufficient to establish shortcut use.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool name can correlate with unsafe while removing it leaves guard decisions unchanged. Evidence of reliance remains insufficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22243-shortcut-sensitivity/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac8c0a7f5918e56a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:shortcut-sensitivity" data-paper-title="Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e1e7f6f866b6b9b">Why not compute F1 per interaction and then average when weighting interactions equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ashortcut-sensitivity">Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kontext</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Assign steps weight 1/n_g, sum weighted TP/TN/FP/FN, then calculate F1. F1 is nonlinear, so averaging group F1s defines another metric. Signed paired effects also cannot be replaced by unsigned flip rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long interactions should not carry more total confusion-matrix weight just because they have more steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22243-shortcut-sensitivity/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e1e7f6f866b6b9b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scipivot" data-paper-title="SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-scipivot-7482a1e6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-011920e64c2ec0a1">Does SciPIvot test research redirection or whether a project ultimately succeeds?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascipivot">SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park / The Chinese University of Hong Kong（PDF上标已核）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It gives the pre-correction project state and two next steps and asks which is more appropriate. The reference comes from later human correction, but the tested model sees no future trajectory or option provenance. This is not prediction of eventual project success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The better next step today does not guarantee a successful project six months later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21082">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21082-scipivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-011920e64c2ec0a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scipivot" data-paper-title="SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9fb1bddc37dbff1d">Why reopen an independent session after swapping options and resample by case rather than answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascipivot">SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park / The Chinese University of Hong Kong（PDF上标已核）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Swapping checks position stability, and separate sessions prevent the first answer from influencing the second. Both orderings still represent one project decision, not independent samples. The model sees only the pre-correction state; later records may build references but cannot be inputs or reveal human versus original LLM authorship.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If plans A and B are presented in both orders in one session, the model may remember the earlier choice instead of judging again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21082">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21082-scipivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9fb1bddc37dbff1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scipivot" data-paper-title="SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0843c04e300f78ca">How does swapping option order differ from treating two answers for the same case as independent samples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascipivot">SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park / The Chinese University of Hong Kong（PDF上标已核）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both orderings measure and offset position bias, but they remain one case. Compute a case score, then resample cases. Counting answers independently inflates sample size and ignores correlation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>AB and BA judgments for one case are not two distinct research decisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21082">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21082-scipivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0843c04e300f78ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scipivot" data-paper-title="SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbb80695c86f30d7">Why not attach SciPIvot&#x27;s original questions file to the evaluated agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascipivot">SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park / The Chinese University of Hong Kong（PDF上标已核）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The official source includes references. Trusted ingestion exports only the ID and two options via an allowlist, storing private grader references separately. Sessions are independent and cannot access repositories or future records to bypass options-only isolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Providing the full questions.json with an instruction not to read references is not data isolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 已发布数据与来源. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21082">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21082-scipivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbb80695c86f30d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:probe" data-paper-title="PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-probe-e4f99af8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-97c88a4c09786eec">Why does PROBE audit policy compliance separately from task completion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprobe">PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final state or harmful-text checks can miss violations during multi-turn tool use. An auditor interacts with a frozen target while a private verifier checks the full trace for business-policy compliance, customer realism, task progress, and coverage rather than tone alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A task can look complete despite missing required confirmation or making an unrequested state change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22124-probe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97c88a4c09786eec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:probe" data-paper-title="PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bbf997d26ce06409">Why decay rewards for repeated violations of the same policy but retain raw yield?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprobe">PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decay prevents the auditor from farming one flaw and encourages policy coverage. Raw yield describes actual events and can exceed 100 per 100 episodes. Report deduplicated coverage separately from event volume. A local reward implementation is not the entire auditing RL pipeline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one conversation triggers a violation three times, give decreasing or zero subsequent reward but preserve all three events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22124-probe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bbf997d26ce06409">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:probe" data-paper-title="PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1e3f83fa2deaa51">Why aren&#x27;t raw violation yield, deduplicated episode-policy yield, and coverage interchangeable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprobe">PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw yield includes repeated turn-level hits and can exceed 100 per 100 episodes. Deduplicated yield removes same-policy repetitions per episode; coverage uses all declared policies as its denominator. They describe hit volume and breadth, not one success probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three hits of one policy in one episode give raw yield 3, deduplicated yield 1, and add only one policy to coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22124-probe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1e3f83fa2deaa51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:probe" data-paper-title="PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4ae230241e88d90">Where must PROBE reset repeated-hit counts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprobe">PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>n_i counts previous hits in the current episode. The first gets weight 1, the second 1/2, and later hits zero; restart each episode. Do not decay raw-yield events, and retain zero-hit and unsupported policies in denominators.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two hits in a previous episode must not turn the first hit of the next episode into zero reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22124-probe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4ae230241e88d90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:librarian-agents" data-paper-title="Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-librarian-agents-828f2c36" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a670d1d22123a010">Why does Librarian organize a workspace before knowing future questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alibrarian-agents">Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A corpus may receive many queries. Hierarchical files and source references amortize organization across documents. The builder sees only the corpus; a frozen answerer later navigates it, without prewriting test answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Organize project files before answering several users, rather than tailoring a directory to a known question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22273-librarian-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a670d1d22123a010">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:librarian-agents" data-paper-title="Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3498243647684558">Why can&#x27;t a builder organize its hierarchical filesystem as an answer index using known evaluation questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alibrarian-agents">Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The aim is a reusable workspace a frozen answerer navigates for unseen queries. Seeing questions early creates answer-oriented shortcuts instead of cross-query organization. Preserve originals for fallback; Delete must not remove raw documents. A general cost formula does not establish nonzero shaping in the main training run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Organizing by company and date supports diverse questions. Placing one anticipated answer on the front page stops the evaluation testing general organization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22273-librarian-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3498243647684558">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:librarian-agents" data-paper-title="Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e1a1b0a38505cf3">Is Librarian&#x27;s general cost utility the same as the paper&#x27;s main training reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alibrarian-agents">Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The general form has build, token, and read penalties, but main training sets them to zero with gamma=1, probes answerability change every eight builder turns, and checks terminal correctness. A definable cost term is not necessarily used for shaping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A token penalty in the formula does not mean this training run deducted reward for reading another file.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22273-librarian-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e1a1b0a38505cf3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:librarian-agents" data-paper-title="Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-58d87f3603156920">How does Librarian preserve provenance after deleting a synthetic node?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alibrarian-agents">Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Delete archives only the synthetic node, promotes its children, and retains raw documents and historical sources. Cold load checks hashes, hierarchy, and disk content. Local work implements filesystem contracts and frozen result recomputation without training a learned builder.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After removing a summary folder, original files and sources for merged subdirectories must remain discoverable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 文件系统合同与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22273-librarian-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58d87f3603156920">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-decomposition" data-paper-title="Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harness-decomposition-8f77338c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee85cdcc7ef9364a">Why does HDA first test paired gain of evolved versus baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-decomposition">Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If the observed gain could be noise, decomposing it into compute, shortcuts, and residual has no reliable starting point. First perform a two-sided paired bootstrap, then build compute-matched and shortcut-neutralized controls only after significance. Both require task-aware human review.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small fluctuations across runs on the same tasks do not justify quantifying generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22466-harness-decomposition/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee85cdcc7ef9364a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-decomposition" data-paper-title="Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c188a5254d4945dd">Why is HDA residual G only an upper bound on generalization improvement, rather than direct transfer evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-decomposition">Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute matching removes extra computation and neutralizing detected shortcuts removes some overfit, but undetected shortcuts can remain. Controls need task-aware human review and attribution starts only after confirming a significant gain. Algebraic accounting does not establish full causal identification or transfer to a new distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing a known filename shortcut may leave gains from hidden directory ordering. Do not call all remaining gains general reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22466-harness-decomposition/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c188a5254d4945dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-decomposition" data-paper-title="Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6815b896a61e9666">Why can&#x27;t HDA&#x27;s residual G be called proven generalization gain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-decomposition">Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is the difference after neutralizing detected shortcuts relative to the compute-matched baseline and may retain unidentified shortcuts, so it is only an upper bound. O covers detected and neutralizable mechanisms, a lower bound on overfit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Gains after eliminating one form of answer leakage do not rule out another shortcut.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22466-harness-decomposition/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6815b896a61e9666">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-decomposition" data-paper-title="Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-375a2b1209b0dd6d">Can negative raw T, O, or G be clipped to zero before displaying HDA percentages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-decomposition">Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Preserve signed raw effects satisfying Delta=T+O+G. Clip display shares only according to their separate rule and do not overwrite original attribution. All four arms must align by item and cost units, with human-reviewed control rationale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If neutralization improves scores, retain negative O instead of setting it to zero for a prettier chart.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22466-harness-decomposition/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-375a2b1209b0dd6d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gacc-bench" data-paper-title="GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-gacc-bench-1c3f337b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a0c53ebe99d3d58">Why does GACC-Bench use one compressed memory for several questions under one goal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agacc-bench">GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only the high-level goal is visible during compression. Reuse checks whether the whole group&#x27;s evidence was retained. Recompressing after seeing a question becomes targeted extraction for a known query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A travel-goal memory should answer both transport and lodging without creating a new summary per question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21893">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21893-gacc-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a0c53ebe99d3d58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gacc-bench" data-paper-title="GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2f9e0b46e42d85cd">Why generate one memory per context–goal–budget and reuse it for all follow-up questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agacc-bench">GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compression sees only the high-level goal, not individual questions. Reuse tests whether one memory retains evidence for the group. Recompressing per question gives the compressor extra query information and changes the task. Strict token truncation, empty memory for zero budget, and no padding determine actual reader inputs, beyond nominal budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A project-decision goal can lead to date and reason questions. Both should read the same precompressed memory, not query-specific summaries extracted later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21893">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21893-gacc-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2f9e0b46e42d85cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gacc-bench" data-paper-title="GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-12efa2fcece6bb35">How can GACC Micro be high while Macro is zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agacc-bench">GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Micro counts correct answers over all questions. Macro scores a goal only when all its questions are correct. Missing one key question in every group can retain high per-question accuracy but zero goal completeness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two goals with two of three questions correct each yield Micro=2/3 and Macro=0.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21893">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21893-gacc-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12efa2fcece6bb35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gacc-bench" data-paper-title="GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce582aebb12bcffd">What should GACC pass to the reader when compressor output exceeds budget or the budget floors to zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agacc-bench">GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the fixed tokenizer to take the first L tokens and decode, without regeneration or padding. L=0 gives empty memory. Bind caches to source, goal, tokenizer, and compressor version so configurations do not share memories incorrectly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With three source tokens and retention 0.2, L=0; do not retain one token to improve scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 代码映射、成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21893">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21893-gacc-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce582aebb12bcffd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:disagreement-routing" data-paper-title="Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-disagreement-routing-3ad2d018" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9fda6925705b314c">Why doesn&#x27;t weak-model uncertainty necessarily justify escalation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adisagreement-routing">Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If the strong model is also unstable on the question, escalation may not improve reliably. Subtract strong self-disagreement from weak–strong disagreement to learn escalation value. Offline equivalence comparisons need no correct-answer labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both models may waver between options. The weak model&#x27;s hesitation alone does not show that the strong model can fix it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22245-disagreement-routing/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9fda6925705b314c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:disagreement-routing" data-paper-title="Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
