<h2 id="qa-15d5ca65c5b0168c">Why subtract strong-model self-disagreement from weak–strong disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adisagreement-routing">Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Disagreement may come from strong-model instability rather than a fixable weak answer. Estimate self-disagreement over distinct sample indices and subtract it for a better escalation signal. The score can be negative and is not a success probability. At test time run only weak representations and probes before paying for escalation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Opposite strong answers make high weak–strong disagreement inconclusive. A consistent strong model disagreeing with the weak one provides a clearer signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22245-disagreement-routing/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15d5ca65c5b0168c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:disagreement-routing" data-paper-title="Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f7410df12418bd1">How does the corrected routing score range differ from raw weak–strong disagreement probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adisagreement-routing">Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw disagreement is a probability. The corrected score subtracts two probe outputs, can be negative, and must not be clipped to [0,1]. Take the minimum response-level prediction across weak answers first, then subtract prompt-level strong self-disagreement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weak–strong disagreement 0.2 and strong self-disagreement 0.5 yield −0.3.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22245-disagreement-routing/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f7410df12418bd1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:disagreement-routing" data-paper-title="Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-53c4ea46a8f59ec0">Why exclude self-pairs when estimating strong-model self-disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adisagreement-routing">Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use K_s(K_s−1) ordered pairs of distinct indices. Diagonal comparisons always agree and bias disagreement down. Calibrate inference thresholds on validation only; under test distribution shift, exact routing quotas are not guaranteed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two strong responses give two ordered cross pairs, not four pairs including both self-pairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22245-disagreement-routing/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53c4ea46a8f59ec0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-perturb" data-paper-title="AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-perturb-def3e837" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8ad67ecaea38b3c">Why does AgentPerturb change only one of U, P, C, or T at a time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-perturb">AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User request, procedure, history/context, and tool contract are distinct input surfaces. Holding others, backend, and success oracle fixed isolates pressure better. Changing several surfaces introduces confounds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A single-target pair can change only tool wording while preserving user requirements and tool implementation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8ad67ecaea38b3c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-perturb" data-paper-title="AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b56c1b86c3904f6">Why independently verify unchanged goals and solvability after perturbations pass JSON checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-perturb">AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Parseable inputs can still change the task or remove essential information. Single-target semantic validation holds other factors, backend, and oracle fixed so differences reflect interaction pressure. Report paired coverage and bounds for missing scores rather than dropping failures and claiming robustness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rewording a tool description should preserve behavior. Removing the only required tool introduces unsolvability, not the same perturbation effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b56c1b86c3904f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-perturb" data-paper-title="AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b7e2047d62548dd">What do AgentPerturb syntax checks and independent semantic verification establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-perturb">AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Syntax checks parseability, not goal preservation or solvability. An independent verifier checks single-target change, unchanged goal, solvability, and executability together with a native validator. A local arithmetic verifier does not prove arbitrary natural-language equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Valid JSON that changes a sum into a product changes the goal and is not a robustness perturbation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 真实性、gold 隔离与成本. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b7e2047d62548dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-perturb" data-paper-title="AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a5927032c165b95">Can AgentPerturb drop unscored requests when calculating paired degradation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-perturb">AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute C, P, and Delta on scored pairs, but report coverage and unknown bounds across all requested pairs. Missing is unknown, and native partial credit must not be arbitrarily binarized to align formats.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only 60 of 100 planned pairs have both scores, do not report just their drop while hiding 40 missing pairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a5927032c165b95">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ctxgap" data-paper-title="What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ctxgap-b6a0f849" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-47dcbdce30974399">How does the CTXGAP reporting gap differ from task completion rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Actxgap">What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It compares cumulative-report and full-execution observers on the same probes, measuring how well users can recover true task state. A completed task can omit key facts in its report; a detailed report does not establish success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Code may be fixed while the report omits an unrun check, leaving users unable to judge acceptance accurately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20003">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20003-ctxgap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47dcbdce30974399">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ctxgap" data-paper-title="What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-823db16c649a2ab8">Why can&#x27;t public execution materials be relabeled T_full to recompute the full report gap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Actxgap">What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The original full view includes some unpublished reasoning or memory evidence. Without it, observer capability and answerable questions change. Pair probes and weight important facts, but separate public and full conditions. Cluster by task/run rather than assuming many probes for one task are independent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a port appears only in private memory, a public-log observer&#x27;s failure cannot represent the original full-view ceiling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与统计单位. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20003">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20003-ctxgap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-823db16c649a2ab8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ctxgap" data-paper-title="What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c679357bfb66ed89">How does CTXGAP importance-weighted accuracy differ from averaging all probes equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Actxgap">What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>More probes in one category should not outweigh another category&#x27;s important facts. Divide the number of important atomic facts by probes in the category, sum weighted scores, and normalize. Equal weighting can let many easy or similar probes hide omissions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many questions about a trivial log should not obscure one missing acceptance fact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与统计单位. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20003">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20003-ctxgap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c679357bfb66ed89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ctxgap" data-paper-title="What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef131aa02e4eacc2">Why resample CTXGAP intervals by task/run rather than individual probes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Actxgap">What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probes within one task share execution and reporting conditions and are not independent. Cluster while keeping paired conditions together. Preserve category weights and equal task aggregation rather than replacing the main gap with pooled accuracy differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A task with 100 similar probes is not 100 independent tasks and should not artificially narrow confidence intervals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与统计单位. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20003">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20003-ctxgap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef131aa02e4eacc2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coda" data-paper-title="Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-coda-3d28333f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9cb6ac979ccc11bc">Why does CODA freeze retrieval before rewriting skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoda">Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Token Hub, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It audits dependence on delivered content and wording. Reretrieval changes selection and ranking, so fix retrieval-side fields and replace content only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a rewritten skill is no longer retrieved, wording dependence cannot be distinguished from recall changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20845">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20845-coda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9cb6ac979ccc11bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coda" data-paper-title="Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2716653480cf5c0">Why freeze the original retrieved skill set before meaning-preserving rewrites?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoda">Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Token Hub, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval could change which skills are delivered, confounding wording sensitivity with ranking. Freeze selected identities and retrieval fields, then change only content. String similarity does not prove semantic equivalence, and unchanged aggregate success can hide bidirectional flips.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Provide the same three skills after paraphrasing. If three different skills are retrieved, outcome changes no longer isolate wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20845">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20845-coda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e2716653480cf5c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coda" data-paper-title="Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-de7e1d0ed3d16d8a">Why does CODA report per-task CR alongside aggregate success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoda">Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Token Hub, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success totals can remain unchanged when some successes become failures and other failures become successes. CR measures agreement across conditions per task; repeated unperturbed runs estimate stochastic noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If success and failure swap across two tasks, total success remains 50% but CR is zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20845">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20845-coda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de7e1d0ed3d16d8a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coda" data-paper-title="Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ba5c0af97c6efeb">Is the number of no-skill successes the CODA RR denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoda">Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Token Hub, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. RR is the proportion of all matched tasks successful under both no-skill and perturbed-skill conditions. Conditioning on successes changes the definition. Keep identical ID sets and reject missing tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Of 100 tasks, 20 no-skill successes and 10 joint successes give RR=10%, not 50%.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20845">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20845-coda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ba5c0af97c6efeb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:alpha-diana" data-paper-title="AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-alpha-diana-d2460928" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-aab95853f7796c15">Why does AlphaDiana separate execution status from grading status?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aalpha-diana">AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong Baptist University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A successful run may lack a valid grader decision. Interrupted grading is unknown, neither correct nor incorrect. Separate statuses and full planned denominators expose execution failures, missing grades, and coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a tool completes but the grader times out, mark ungraded rather than removing the sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20675-alpha-diana/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aab95853f7796c15">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:alpha-diana" data-paper-title="AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5990e05270ed514c">Why do retries add attempts without adding logical samples or choosing the best result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aalpha-diana">AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong Baptist University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retries of a task/sample address the same request. Changing denominators or selecting the best attempt distorts sampling and hides failure costs. Report the latest record and sum costs over attempts; separate execution and grading. Ungraded is unknown, not correct or silently excluded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a task times out then succeeds, charge both attempts&#x27; tokens while retaining one sample. Do not keep only the cheap success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20675-alpha-diana/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5990e05270ed514c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:alpha-diana" data-paper-title="AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7a972d5c6d3a5f6">What evaluation difference arises from selecting the latest rather than best retry?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aalpha-diana">AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong Baptist University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retries leave the logical denominator unchanged, and the protocol reports latest status. Best-of selection introduces an implicit extra-attempt advantage. Costs accumulate across every attempt, not only the one shown.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a success is followed by a failed retry, latest-status reporting cannot restore the earlier success and charge only one execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20675-alpha-diana/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7a972d5c6d3a5f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:alpha-diana" data-paper-title="AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4b3a77db599905fc">When must AlphaDiana return unknown for complete tokens per correct result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aalpha-diana">AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong Baptist University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Return None if there are no confirmed correct samples, any attempt lacks token counts, or any requested sample lacks execution records. Report known tokens and coverage separately; partial measurement is not complete cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one of two attempts has no token count, even an eventual correct result cannot establish full cost per correct sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 无 gold 边界与限制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20675-alpha-diana/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4b3a77db599905fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:clasharness" data-paper-title="CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-clasharness-f0eec5c3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5739ffdb20a3b64a">Why does CLASHarness execute a reference plan before agents handle conflicting messages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aclasharness">CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Emory University（共同署名）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference execution verifies solvability under fixed true state and compiles checks from observed effects. Otherwise failure may reflect a broken scenario, not inability to handle false facts, stale state, or conflicting peer instructions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a peer claims a file changed, verify actual state and a reachable goal first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.19128-clasharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5739ffdb20a3b64a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:clasharness" data-paper-title="CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c034b18ddbd1802">Why fix true state and run a reference plan to prove solvability before generating conflict scenarios?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aclasharness">CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Emory University（共同署名）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise failures may stem from contradictions or an unusable interface rather than peer-conflict handling. Executable references establish true state, permitted goals, and obligations, then evaluation tests whether the agent finishes from the environment. Empty requirements or missing verdicts are not automatic success, and fairness adjustments must be preregistered.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A peer may claim a file was deleted while it still exists and the reference can complete the task. This tests whether the agent checks the environment rather than facing an impossible case.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与公平性口径. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.19128-clasharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c034b18ddbd1802">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:clasharness" data-paper-title="CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf253b82e67b2178">Why report CLASHarness complete success separately from partial check pass rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aclasharness">CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Emory University（共同署名）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Complete success requires a verified nonempty required list with every item passed. Partial rate reports how many checks passed. An empty conjunction or incomplete verdict list does not establish full success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Passing three of four required checks gives 75% partial credit and no complete success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与公平性口径. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.19128-clasharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf253b82e67b2178">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:clasharness" data-paper-title="CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-751859fe4985dd0e">Why shouldn&#x27;t CLASHarness match records by list position when downgrading checks for fairness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aclasharness">CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Emory University（共同署名）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identify checks by original task_id/check_index, mark specified required items diagnostic, and union overlapping categories. Reordering or duplicate labels can cause wrong removals or double counts if based on positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A check in two disputed categories should appear only once in the downgrade set.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与公平性口径. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.19128-clasharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-751859fe4985dd0e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:option-channel-attack" data-paper-title="One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-option-channel-attack-6cce967b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-33342ffea93fc28c">Why can Option-Channel Attack change a guard decision by altering only labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoption-channel-attack">One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Typed-output names also enter the model. Misleading labels can affect the mapping from an unchanged action to allow or deny, exposing the option-name channel while trusted policy and actions stay fixed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The meaning of allow and deny is unchanged, but caller-supplied names can induce the wrong choice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12292-option-channel-attack/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-33342ffea93fc28c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:option-channel-attack" data-paper-title="One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e849af5852a4fa5">Why can changing only option labels affect guard approval while actions and trusted policy remain fixed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoption-channel-attack">One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Labels are model inputs and their semantics can affect typed output selection without action changes. Separate unsafe approvals from benign denials. Conditional attack rate uses prohibited examples correctly rejected on clean inputs; an empty denominator is undefined, not zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A misleading label for &#x27;deny&#x27; can change the model&#x27;s choice for the same prohibited call without changing the actual policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12292-option-channel-attack/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e849af5852a4fa5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:option-channel-attack" data-paper-title="One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1c21f0da9acb53da">Why not combine fail-open and fail-closed into one safety accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoption-channel-attack">One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fail-open admits prohibited actions; fail-closed denies permitted actions. Safety and usability effects differ. Conditional ASR applies only to clean correctly rejected cases and cannot replace overall error rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rejecting everything can reduce unsafe approvals while making legitimate tasks unusable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12292-option-channel-attack/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1c21f0da9acb53da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:option-channel-attack" data-paper-title="One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4bff9ac6252201f">What is conditional ASR when no clean example was correctly rejected?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoption-channel-attack">One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Undefined because the denominator is empty; do not report zero or one. Recompute the conditional denominator in each paired bootstrap draw. Select attack labels on calibration and measure on separate evaluation data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model already incorrectly approving every case offers no clean rejection that could flip to approval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 代码映射与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12292-option-channel-attack/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4bff9ac6252201f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ontrack" data-paper-title="OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ontrack-56d9bc62" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-23e3166f678480f8">Why does OnTrack represent trajectories as dependency graphs rather than compare action text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aontrack">OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cribl AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Order and artifact dependencies determine deviation, and independent branches may have different valid orders. Structured unbalanced alignment allows partial prefix/reference matches. Without a reference, explicitly fall back to loop, retry, and stagnation signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapping the order of two independent files should not be labeled deviation merely because indices change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12375-ontrack/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-23e3166f678480f8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ontrack" data-paper-title="OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-655da0c786f78c79">Why not rescale old prefix-node mass to 1/t whenever a new event arrives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aontrack">OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cribl AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rescaling changes historical weights merely because the stream grows, confounding progress with normalization. Fixed prefix mass, streaming warm starts, and structural coupling preserve comparisons over time. Before intervening, increase the solver budget and recompute; irreversible-action gates cannot rely on stale frontier caches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new log read should not automatically reduce the mass of an earlier critical edit. Otherwise a score change can come from the denominator rather than actual drift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12375-ontrack/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-655da0c786f78c79">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ontrack" data-paper-title="OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5d972834c027596">Why use different weights for OnTrack&#x27;s early exploration grace and final alignment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aontrack">OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cribl AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Online new nodes receive age discount and a frontier mask to avoid premature penalties. At termination, cold-start without these adjustments to check the complete trace. Keeping exploration grace in final scores can hide unresolved drift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A temporary artifact gets early grace, but if still unused at termination it needs full review.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12375-ontrack/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5d972834c027596">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ontrack" data-paper-title="OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cba62001fc682760">May OnTrack reset existing node mass from 1/m to 1/t at each event?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aontrack">OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cribl AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Agent nodes receive fixed prefix mass 1/m_bar. Rescaling changes old masses and leakage conventions. Recompute the frontier with current coupling before irreversible actions. Planner references can warn but cannot automatically halt execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One unrelated new event should not lower all prior masses solely by changing a denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.12375-ontrack/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cba62001fc682760">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:specguard" data-paper-title="SpecGuard: Proving a Task Is Broken Before the Agent Cheats" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-specguard-31696f7e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b4123e304451411">Why doesn&#x27;t SpecGuard let SpecAgent see tests?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspecguard">SpecGuard: Proving a Task Is Broken Before the Agent Cheats</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MATS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tests may conflict with trusted task descriptions; copying them into intent would prove only the tests&#x27; own requirements. SpecAgent sees description and code, TestAgent translates independently, and Lean checks conflict after semantic connection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the description says add one but tests demand 2 become 4, do not write &#x27;2 becomes 4&#x27; into the intent specification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09159">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.09159-specguard/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b4123e304451411">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:specguard" data-paper-title="SpecGuard: Proving a Task Is Broken Before the Agent Cheats" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-837e8a2527eb3a28">Why can a Lean proof still yield inconclusive even though SpecAgent never sees tests?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspecguard">SpecGuard: Proving a Task Is Broken Before the Agent Cheats</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MATS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Test isolation keeps intent independent of potentially wrong or malicious requirements, and the Certifier checks conflict. A proof applies only to translations and connector expressions. If natural-language meaning cannot be aligned faithfully, kernel success does not prove the original task is corrupted; keep inconclusive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sorting versus reverse-order requirements can be formalized as a conflict. Ambiguity over &#x27;stable sorting&#x27; should not be settled solely by a limited proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09159">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.09159-specguard/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-837e8a2527eb3a28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:specguard" data-paper-title="SpecGuard: Proving a Task Is Broken Before the Agent Cheats" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-55dce45e534cd4ad">Does a Lean-kernel conflict certificate prove that the original natural-language task must conflict?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspecguard">SpecGuard: Proving a Task Is Broken Before the Agent Cheats</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MATS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It establishes no common implementation for the generated specification and test constraints, not faithful translation. Semantic connection or intent extraction may be wrong. Allow inconclusive when expression or alignment fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A proof obtained after translating &#x27;add one&#x27; as &#x27;add two&#x27; does not validate the original task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果与验收边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09159">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.09159-specguard/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-55dce45e534cd4ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:specguard" data-paper-title="SpecGuard: Proving a Task Is Broken Before the Agent Cheats" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a583d933cd754ee0">Does a passed SpecGuard A100 receipt show real end-to-end model success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspecguard">SpecGuard: Proving a Task Is Broken Before the Agent Cheats</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MATS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. All three archived small-model cases were inconclusive with zero conflict certificates and stopped at Spec. Passed verifies real CUDA execution and provenance. Handwritten Lean passes test mechanics, not model output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A working GPU command and saved failures do not establish that the model reached TestAgent and connector stages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 结果与验收边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09159">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.09159-specguard/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a583d933cd754ee0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:veriharness" data-paper-title="VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-veriharness-6d6ee53b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f8826a9c4da28bf9">Why does VeriHarness challenge consensus as well as resolve disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Averiharness">VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiple matching answers can share missing evidence or omitted requirements. The resolver investigates disputed claims; the challenger questions shared claims and gaps. Evidence tools and workspaces keep agreement from substituting for correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three agents can cite the same unchecked claim, which still needs verification despite unanimous votes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00972-veriharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f8826a9c4da28bf9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:veriharness" data-paper-title="VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2be905d50052cea6">Why add a consensus challenger after multiple verifiers agree?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Averiharness">VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Consensus can share mistakes or omissions. Resolving explicit disagreement cannot find requirements everyone skipped. The challenger questions consensus and gaps; the resolver gathers evidence for conflicts. Use evidence tools rather than majority counts as truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If three reviewers inspect screenshots but none examines downloaded files, the challenger can flag missing artifact review even without disagreement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00972-veriharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2be905d50052cea6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:veriharness" data-paper-title="VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce48a1617a5b524b">How does VeriHarness evidence scoring differ from simple majority voting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Averiharness">VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Voting counts opinions. The score also considers supporting evidence, contradictions involving consensus, and a claim-count penalty. More votes or claims do not improve verifiability automatically. The local fixture checker is not the paper&#x27;s actual tool environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One precise, supported claim can be preferable to ten repeated but contradictory claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00972-veriharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce48a1617a5b524b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:veriharness" data-paper-title="VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b27b377f2f75b895">Why record claim segmentation when implementing the VeriHarness claim-count penalty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Averiharness">VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The score includes epsilon times claim count, so splitting or merging content changes the penalty. Preserve support, contradiction, and count to explain selection. Fixture verdicts are not real-world fact verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Splitting one sentence into three claims changes the penalty; use consistent segmentation across candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00972-veriharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b27b377f2f75b895">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:safe-self-improvement" data-paper-title="Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-safe-self-improvement-450abfd4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-62d68c3d6cbc7b8d">Why does Safe Self-Improvement distinguish the next edit source from the current implementation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asafe-self-improvement">Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A program can be a useful starting point without meeting current execution conditions. Detection, executable selection, and edit-source selection are separate, and candidates are revalidated under current conditions so old passes do not conceal current failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Useful code from an old version does not make the entire version safe to run today.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01073-safe-self-improvement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62d68c3d6cbc7b8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:safe-self-improvement" data-paper-title="Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-48504ee29677188e">Why select the currently executable version separately from the next edit source?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asafe-self-improvement">Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A promising edit parent may not run safely under present conditions. Revalidate execution candidates and select from the qualified set. If none pass, return to founder rather than using a failed incumbent. Restoring execution and continuing search differ, and historical passes are not permanent eligibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep a failed incumbent for edit analysis if useful, but execute a currently qualified version or roll back to founder.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01073-safe-self-improvement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48504ee29677188e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:safe-self-improvement" data-paper-title="Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-83fc9f453ef86614">How does founder rollback differ from continuing with the incumbent when nothing passes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asafe-self-improvement">Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select the highest score only among currently valid candidates. If none qualify, roll back to founder. Continuing with a failed incumbent bypasses validation; rollback is a recovery protocol, not proof founder is always safe in any new condition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A top-scoring candidate that currently fails cannot keep the execution role on the strength of past scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01073-safe-self-improvement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83fc9f453ef86614">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
