<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:safe-self-improvement" data-paper-title="Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c9e0f5c5a680555c">Can Safe Self-Improvement reuse a candidate&#x27;s previous pass flag directly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asafe-self-improvement">Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Recheck current conditions and choose the highest-scoring current pass. The local path executes verification and founder fallback selection, without the paper&#x27;s edit model or Bedrock experiments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changed tool permissions or task conditions invalidate unconditional reuse of an old passed flag.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01073-safe-self-improvement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c9e0f5c5a680555c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pace-capability" data-paper-title="PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-pace-capability-eec90992" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea936171a3e8d4b0">Why does PACE check capability and provenance before tool side effects?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apace-capability">PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trusted stored material does not grant authority for every action. Derive authority from authenticated requests and check it with input provenance before each effect, preventing low-trust content from expanding permissions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A webpage saying &#x27;send the file&#x27; is not user authorization to send it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01349">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01349-pace-capability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea936171a3e8d4b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pace-capability" data-paper-title="PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ab360b3ac4766b4">Why doesn&#x27;t safe memory ingestion guarantee that its content has authority at execution time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apace-capability">PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ingestion checks content then; execution also limits real effects under the authenticated request and verifies trusted provenance. Both authority and provenance must pass so untrusted memory cannot use a legitimate tool beyond scope. Text claiming authorization does not replace system authentication or per-effect checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A stored webpage that says to delete files does not authorize deletion, even if ingestion found no danger. Check effects and provenance before execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01349">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01349-pace-capability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ab360b3ac4766b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pace-capability" data-paper-title="PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9838b220b0dc8012">Can PACE use capability or provenance checks alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apace-capability">PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Allow an effect only if authority covers it and provenance is trusted. Capability limits what can be done; provenance checks whether the present basis is trustworthy. Both are required.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>General file-read permission does not imply approving this specific read instruction from an untrusted page.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01349">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01349-pace-capability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9838b220b0dc8012">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pace-capability" data-paper-title="PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b7efda99a1c0174">Can PACE execute a tool first and apply the gate later from logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apace-capability">PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A pre-effect gate must obtain the complete effect set before execution and compare authority and provenance. Later logs only audit; they cannot undo effects. The local path tests selection without operating system or browser tools.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Finding untrusted provenance after an email is sent misses the opportunity to prevent it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01349">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01349-pace-capability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b7efda99a1c0174">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:defa" data-paper-title="DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-defa-2f35dc42" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-51e5a476da3647c4">Why does DeFA trace backward along dependencies from the final violation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adefa">DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The last error may be downstream of a propagated mistake. Combine protocol and semantic relationships into an event graph, trace the source, and retain downstream propagation and responsible agent to distinguish trigger from decisive error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The deploying agent is not necessarily at fault if earlier configuration was written incorrectly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01256-defa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51e5a476da3647c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:defa" data-paper-title="DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6828861af8c1cd51">Why retain the propagation subgraph when locating a decisive error instead of labeling only the last failed action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adefa">DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final failure may stem from earlier facts, parameters, or agent messages. Backward dependencies connect the source with affected nodes. Protocol relations give structure and semantic dependencies capture information flow. Maximum error scores still need evidence and do not prove complete causality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Deployment can fail because an early read used stale configuration. A propagation graph follows stale fields into the final arguments instead of blaming only deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01256-defa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6828861af8c1cd51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:defa" data-paper-title="DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb7cdb92ee87b5d4">How does DeFA choose a decisive error differently from taking the last failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adefa">DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It selects by error magnitude among ancestors of the violation and retains responsibility and propagation. The last event is just a time position. Graph selection depends on supplied edges and error definition, not independent causal proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A final retry timeout may be a symptom of wrong parameters generated earlier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01256-defa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb7cdb92ee87b5d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:defa" data-paper-title="DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e222262e26ccc6c9">Why retain dependencies and responsibility rather than only event text in DeFA propagation graphs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adefa">DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidates come from Ancestor(V); missing edges hide upstream sources and wrong edges add unrelated events. Preserve protocol/semantic dependencies, event IDs, error magnitudes, and responsible agents. The local path reads no gold plan and runs no multimodal judge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If two agents write a file, trace the specific version consumed by the failure to identify the relevant write.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01256-defa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e222262e26ccc6c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:user-proxy-bench" data-paper-title="UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-user-proxy-bench-da315c41" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb83180f6993ea13">Why does UserProxyBench separate simulator fidelity from task reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Auser-proxy-bench">UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Simulators can leak private fields and let agents succeed with less information collection. Independent UFS checks every user contract, avoiding misreading reward on an easier task as real interaction ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unrequested hidden order number can enable success without showing strong clarification ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38043-userproxybench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb83180f6993ea13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:user-proxy-bench" data-paper-title="UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9940179a02b78e4">Why can premature disclosure by a user simulator improve task success but reduce UFS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Auser-proxy-bench">UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The agent should ask for information, and unsolicited disclosure bypasses that capability. UFS separately checks every applicable user contract per episode rather than reusing task reward. Completion and fidelity are distinct; success alone does not establish simulator quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Giving an order number before being asked may make refunds succeed without testing whether the agent knew when to request it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38043-userproxybench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9940179a02b78e4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:user-proxy-bench" data-paper-title="UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-29e12f69eb102a9b">How does the UFS all-criteria product differ from averaging criterion pass rates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Auser-proxy-bench">UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An episode scores one only when all applicable criteria pass; any failure gives zero. Per-criterion means can let other passes offset a key violation and are a different metric. Report UFS separately from task reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Passing nine of ten criteria gives 90% per-criterion average but strict UFS zero for that episode.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38043-userproxybench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29e12f69eb102a9b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:user-proxy-bench" data-paper-title="UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4ac506d1471107c">Why retain the order of request and disclosure when auditing premature disclosure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Auser-proxy-bench">UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prematurity depends on whether the relevant request came first, not whether a field eventually appears. Local evaluation checks public interaction events against the rubric while keeping private blueprints on the grading side. It does not run paper enterprise tasks or the closed-proxy matrix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Disclosing the same field before or after a question can leave identical final text but different fidelity verdicts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38043-userproxybench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4ac506d1471107c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:certified-selective-eval" data-paper-title="Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-certified-selective-eval-1bfcfcb0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-03ef9bb812f4f600">Why can selective automated evaluation defer some cases to people?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acertified-selective-eval">Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The aim is to automate reliable regions within a certified error budget, not apply machine judgments to every trace. If the upper confidence bound fails the budget, retain human or other evaluation. Report coverage together with risk.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Automate clear cases while routing ambiguous ones to reviewers; accuracy on automated cases alone is incomplete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:certified-selective-eval" data-paper-title="Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a0d4910bf52da75">Why bootstrap by task clusters for an automated-region error certificate instead of treating all traces as independent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acertified-selective-eval">Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Traces from the same task share difficulty and structure, so independent resampling understates correlation and uncertainty. Cluster sampling builds an error upper bound; automate only below budget, with human or external review otherwise. Low average error does not certify arbitrary thresholds, and the certificate depends on calibration distribution and selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hundred similar traces from one task are not a hundred independent successes. Resample them as one task cluster.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34320">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.34320-certified-selective-eval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a0d4910bf52da75">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:certified-selective-eval" data-paper-title="Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a5b687bab96bef57">What does an error upper confidence bound control beyond empirical error in the automated region?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acertified-selective-eval">Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Empirical error summarizes observed samples, while the upper bound reflects uncertainty from finite evidence. Automate only below budget; even zero observed errors can be insufficient. Certification concerns risk in the selected region, not guaranteed correctness on every item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>No observed errors in a small region does not imply a low enough upper bound or justify expanding coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34320">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.34320-certified-selective-eval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a5b687bab96bef57">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:certified-selective-eval" data-paper-title="Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-20ce56f5e0218ac3">Can the local bootstrap certificate be reported as coverage on the paper&#x27;s corpus?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acertified-selective-eval">Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The mini-suite tests clustered resampling and the upper-bound takeover rule. Fix traceable task identities, automated regions, and error labels. The confidence bound rather than point error must satisfy budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Low sample error with a high bound does not establish that the error budget is met.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34320">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.34320-certified-selective-eval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-20ce56f5e0218ac3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-design-study" data-paper-title="An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harness-design-study-2ead25c3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cbb02b7c2b56112">What decisions outside the model does the harness encompass in a harness design study?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-design-study">An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts Amherst</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It organizes planning, available actions, and context management and executes tasks through an underlying loop. These are workflow decisions, not model-weight changes. Identifying editable components explains why the same model behaves differently under different execution designs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One coding model may see a single file fragment or compressed context from several files. That is a harness change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.20804-harness-design-study/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cbb02b7c2b56112">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-design-study" data-paper-title="An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d229d83150e67e88">Why vary planning, action space, and context separately while fixing the execution loop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-design-study">An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts Amherst</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-harness comparisons change many factors, confounding more reasoning, easier actions, and improved state management. Control components separately under the same loop and evaluate effects and costs. References or statistical contracts do not run the paper&#x27;s large coding workloads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Change only the editor to precise replacement while keeping prompts and budgets fixed, rather than crediting a simultaneous model change to the action space.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.20804-harness-design-study/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d229d83150e67e88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-design-study" data-paper-title="An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-874a1ff3f39097e6">Why not combine more detailed planning and a richer action space into one improvement claim?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-design-study">An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts Amherst</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They affect cost and behavior through different pathways. A combined change does not reveal individual contributions; controlled factors are needed, and interactions may occur. Do not assign a combined gain to one component.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Success after adding both planning and tools does not tell which helped most.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.20804-harness-design-study/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-874a1ff3f39097e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-design-study" data-paper-title="An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fe97b28686a5cbea">Does testing controllable local harness factors mean SWE-bench was run?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-design-study">An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts Amherst</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The mini-suite verifies factors and control flow. Keep model version, budget, and tool protocol fixed, and do not report benchmark capability without actual tasks and execution evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A simulated tool success cannot be converted into a real repository repair rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.20804-harness-design-study/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fe97b28686a5cbea">Question link</a></p>
