<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:fuse-evaluator" data-paper-title="Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-fuse-evaluator-e12e2808" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-64902b38498f512a">Does FUSE train a social agent or provide a verifiable social-reasoning evaluation environment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afuse-evaluator">Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Hebrew University of Jerusalem / University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is an evaluation: a multi-agent simulation with verifiable hidden motives tests how assistants interpret user retellings and social context. Hidden state supplies grading evidence, not assistant answers. Implementing the simulator or local kernel does not train a stronger social reasoner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The simulation knows a character&#x27;s true intent, while the assistant judges from the retelling. The evaluator checks afterward without revealing it first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17496-fuse-evaluator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64902b38498f512a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:fuse-evaluator" data-paper-title="Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a95517ba8ccb520">Why are verifiable hidden motives better for social-reasoning evaluation than judging the fluency of retellings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afuse-evaluator">Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Hebrew University of Jerusalem / University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retellings can be biased or incomplete. Fluent replies may not identify real goals. A simulator keeps motives and event conditions hidden from the actor and uses them to check inferences rather than textual agreement. Only the verifier sees references, and fixed fixtures are not actual multi-agent semantic interaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user calls a coworker&#x27;s refusal hostility while the simulated cause is a resource conflict. Evaluate whether the assistant distinguishes them from visible evidence rather than echoing the framing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17496-fuse-evaluator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a95517ba8ccb520">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:fuse-evaluator" data-paper-title="Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e2c04c08d3994d6">How does a framing-bias evaluation differ from ordinary QA accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afuse-evaluator">Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Hebrew University of Jerusalem / University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Framing can influence attribution even with unchanged facts. Comparing retellings against hidden state measures shifts in social judgment. Small simulated state machines do not establish comprehensive real-world social understanding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Describing the same lateness as indifference or a traffic delay can change the assistant&#x27;s judgment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17496-fuse-evaluator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e2c04c08d3994d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:fuse-evaluator" data-paper-title="Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e135e56517048e10">What boundaries did the local FUSE evaluator execute, and did it call twelve external LLMs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afuse-evaluator">Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Hebrew University of Jerusalem / University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It runs only an observation-safe evaluation state machine, not the external model matrix. Project public observations separately from private motives; never pass an internal object containing gold to the actor callback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The grader may know the actual relationship without exposing that field in the assistant input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17496-fuse-evaluator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e135e56517048e10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:silr" data-paper-title="SiLR: Structure-Preserving Admission and Process Reward for LLM Tool Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-silr-f498d510" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f68f6731f7ec1f4">Does SiLR shadow execution undo actions after real execution fails?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asilr">SiLR: Structure-Preserving Admission and Process Reward for LLM Tool Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Science Tokyo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It evaluates proposed state effects on a shadow path before a gate admits real execution. Separate proposal assessment from real effects; executing first cannot establish prevention, especially for irreversible effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Simulate which constraints a configuration edit touches before committing, rather than breaking the configuration and then attempting rollback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04629-silr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f68f6731f7ec1f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:silr" data-paper-title="SiLR: Structure-Preserving Admission and Process Reward for LLM Tool Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e48dd4d8eb6dd50">Why shouldn&#x27;t a safety gate reject every action that leaves any residual violation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asilr">SiLR: Structure-Preserving Admission and Process Reward for LLM Tool Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Science Tokyo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recovery can require intermediate states that remain partly unsafe. Rejecting all of them can deadlock the system. SiLR shadow-executes and requires every constrained branch not to worsen, allowing gradual improvement. A total can hide branch regressions, and shadow outcomes must match real execution contracts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Revoke one of two problematic permissions first. The system remains imperfect but improves; requiring all violations to disappear in one step can block recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04629-silr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e48dd4d8eb6dd50">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:silr" data-paper-title="SiLR: Structure-Preserving Admission and Process Reward for LLM Tool Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-28c3f5f612d987c1">How does product order differ from adding violation severities into one score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asilr">SiLR: Structure-Preserving Admission and Process Reward for LLM Tool Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Science Tokyo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Componentwise non-worsening prevents improvement on one branch from offsetting deterioration on another. A scalar can hide that exchange. Preserve constraints; a weighted sum is not an equivalent safety gate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Storage savings do not justify expanded permissions even if a combined score decreases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04629-silr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28c3f5f612d987c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:silr" data-paper-title="SiLR: Structure-Preserving Admission and Process Reward for LLM Tool Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4644d5aa5ea7b39">Can SiLR substitute an unreliable simulator for real effects during shadow execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asilr">SiLR: Structure-Preserving Admission and Process Reward for LLM Tool Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Science Tokyo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not as a safety claim. Admission requires deterministic, adequately covering verification. Shadow first, compare states, then execute. Without a real simulator, local checks establish only structured criteria and process signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If shadowing omits deletion side effects, an unchanged vector can conceal actual risk.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04629-silr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4644d5aa5ea7b39">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:redevoagent" data-paper-title="RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-redevoagent-15b9a312" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ca939019ba0967a7">Why does RedEvoAgent distill experience into skills rather than store whole traces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aredevoagent">RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long traces contain noise and consume context. Readable abstract skills improve reuse, and tool credit focuses on decisive steps. Abstraction can lose detail, so skills require held-out validation before promotion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Extract &#x27;verify permission boundaries first&#x27; from a long investigation rather than copying every irrelevant attempt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27439-redevoagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ca939019ba0967a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:redevoagent" data-paper-title="RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7faccca6551b9dd">Why must an experience skill beat the incumbent on a holdout rather than just come from a successful audit trace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aredevoagent">RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The original success supports only one context. Abstraction may overfit wording or credit irrelevant tools. Holdout comparison measures reuse, and only strict gains replace an incumbent to prevent low-quality accumulation. Readable skills still need real execution; a local filter is not full evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An audit skill that succeeds on its original example but fails on related unseen cases should not become the default.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27439-redevoagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7faccca6551b9dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:redevoagent" data-paper-title="RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e61370a89e35777a">How does attributing only decisive tools differ from crediting every tool in a successful trace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aredevoagent">RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trace success does not mean each call contributed. Equal credit can fossilize irrelevant steps into skills. Decisive attribution retains experiences that change audit outcomes, reducing library noise. An attribution score does not establish a universal causal law.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An irrelevant lookup before a decisive tool should not become a required skill simply because the trace succeeded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27439-redevoagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e61370a89e35777a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:redevoagent" data-paper-title="RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e193e5815d941ea">Has RedEvoAgent locally red-teamed an actual product?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aredevoagent">RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A safety mini-suite checks attribution and skill-update control flow. Replaying public artifacts is not a new external attack. Record skill provenance, evaluation splits, and replacement evidence without calling replay fresh execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Loading an existing result confirms the protocol can be read, not that an attack just occurred.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27439-redevoagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e193e5815d941ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spec-driven-tests" data-paper-title="Grounding AI Agents in Contracts: An Empirical Evaluation of Spec-Driven Test Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-spec-driven-tests-4c06eb29" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1fb84391154bc6c">What do Pre, Post, and Sug mean in specification-driven testing, and can suggestions replace behavior contracts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspec-driven-tests">Grounding AI Agents in Contracts: An Empirical Evaluation of Spec-Driven Test Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pre defines conditions before a call. Post specifies behavior given those conditions. Sug suggests verification. Suggestions are not contracts; define valid inputs and outcomes first, then mark tested and untested conditions to identify omissions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For sorting, Pre may require comparable elements, Post requires order and element preservation, and Sug proposes duplicate and empty-list tests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17177v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.17177-spec-driven-tests/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1fb84391154bc6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spec-driven-tests" data-paper-title="Grounding AI Agents in Contracts: An Empirical Evaluation of Spec-Driven Test Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d27f4aa512ac8b25">Why does writing preconditions and postconditions first expose coverage gaps missed by direct test generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspec-driven-tests">Grounding AI Agents in Contracts: An Empirical Evaluation of Spec-Driven Test Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Specifications list input restrictions and guaranteed behavior per unit, then mark tested and untested items so tests target auditable coverage. Source interpretation can still be unfaithful. The paper&#x27;s automated comparison did not include human edits, so don&#x27;t treat optional developer steps as executed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A specification can flag empty input returning an empty list as an untested postcondition, whereas copying normal examples can miss it indefinitely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17177v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.17177-spec-driven-tests/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d27f4aa512ac8b25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spec-driven-tests" data-paper-title="Grounding AI Agents in Contracts: An Empirical Evaluation of Spec-Driven Test Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6cc9079f0e3f1ce6">How does fixed-source input differ from exposing historical bugs to test generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspec-driven-tests">Grounding AI Agents in Contracts: An Empirical Evaluation of Spec-Driven Test Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The generator sees only repaired source and public requirements; the private evaluator uses buggy versions. Old patches or bug locations change difficulty and no longer test discovery under the same protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing which line broke supports targeted tests, not independent contract inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17177v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.17177-spec-driven-tests/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6cc9079f0e3f1ce6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spec-driven-tests" data-paper-title="Grounding AI Agents in Contracts: An Empirical Evaluation of Spec-Driven Test Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7c7b70e668e862c">Does compilation failure or modifying source count as bug detection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspec-driven-tests">Grounding AI Agents in Contracts: An Empirical Evaluation of Spec-Driven Test Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The same test must compile and pass on fixed code and compile but fail a real assertion on buggy code. Illegal file edits invalidate runs; use an external trusted diff, not self-reports.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An intentional call to a nonexistent API that breaks old compilation is not a valid regression test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17177v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.17177-spec-driven-tests/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7c7b70e668e862c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessopt-bench" data-paper-title="HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harnessopt-bench-502f5ddb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b32f7ffe5fc0c451">What may HarnessOpt-Bench optimize, and does that include retraining the base model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessopt-bench">HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It searches prompt, tools, control flow, and memory under a target-evaluation budget. Arbitrary base-model retraining or hidden training data are not the same search space. Record candidate versions and allowed edit scope.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A search can try context compression, but replacing the base with a stronger model confounds harness gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06301-harnessopt-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b32f7ffe5fc0c451">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessopt-bench" data-paper-title="HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3dd81229ff5366d7">Why fix target-evaluation budget instead of comparing the highest final score alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessopt-bench">HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>More evaluations create more search opportunities and confound optimizer quality with resources. Hidden tests isolate selection, while trusted environments and version records audit changes. Relative gains depend on baseline scale; the best visible search score is not final unseen performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An optimizer that tries a thousand candidates versus ten is not necessarily better because its best is higher. Match call budgets first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06301-harnessopt-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3dd81229ff5366d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessopt-bench" data-paper-title="HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-726b6cc81a06976f">Why separate open search feedback from hidden test?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessopt-bench">HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search uses visible feedback to choose versions, while hidden evaluation measures generalization. Repeatedly reading test during search turns it into tuning data; score gains no longer reflect unseen ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing the highest test score after dozens of variants overstates performance on unseen tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06301-harnessopt-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-726b6cc81a06976f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessopt-bench" data-paper-title="HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b98c65c6671a3fc9">Can local candidate registration replace trusted execution and version audit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessopt-bench">HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Count real budget, snapshot candidates, and isolate execution. Do not report benchmark scores without the actual model and environment. Define epsilon for relative gains near a zero baseline rather than silently changing the denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding a configuration name does not mean the optimizer changed and tested it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06301-harnessopt-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b98c65c6671a3fc9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:os-shepherd" data-paper-title="OSReward / OS-Shepherd" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-os-shepherd-3f53da9c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-08f584e8368a5348">Does OS-Shepherd operate the computer or judge trajectory success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aos-shepherd">OSReward / OS-Shepherd</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It judges complete computer-operation traces. The evaluated actor clicks and types. OSReward provides human-verified tasks and trajectories for testing reward models. Do not confuse recognizing success with performing the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The actor attempts to save a file and the judge checks the trace. A correct verdict does not mean the judge saved it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28609">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28609-osreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-08f584e8368a5348">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:os-shepherd" data-paper-title="OSReward / OS-Shepherd" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc27e01fb888a3e5">Why can ordinary accuracy conceal a reward model that predicts almost everything successful?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aos-shepherd">OSReward / OS-Shepherd</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>With many successes, approving every trace can score well while missing actual failures. Report success recall, failure recall, and their mean. Cross-system and hard-subset conclusions need real labels; interface diagnostics do not measure open judge capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At 90% successes, predicting all successes gives 90% accuracy and zero failure recall, so balanced accuracy is only 50%.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28609">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28609-osreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc27e01fb888a3e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:os-shepherd" data-paper-title="OSReward / OS-Shepherd" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-54e6b7d5ed63c0ae">How does a judge reading the last five states plus text history differ from using only the final screenshot?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aos-shepherd">OSReward / OS-Shepherd</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A final image can omit process and implicit requirements, while history supplies evidence but also noise. An arbitrary summary changes the observation protocol and is not directly comparable with the paper&#x27;s scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An open window at the end does not show that prior file edits were saved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28609">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28609-osreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54e6b7d5ed63c0ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:os-shepherd" data-paper-title="OSReward / OS-Shepherd" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-833109ee45e06251">Did the local OSReward path train an open 9B or 35B vision judge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aos-shepherd">OSReward / OS-Shepherd</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It did not download official screenshot trajectories either; it only implements the evaluation contract. Join predictions with human labels on the grading side. Explicitly report empty class denominators rather than filling fake balanced accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A batch with no failures cannot estimate failure recall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28609">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28609-osreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-833109ee45e06251">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:finance-harness-protocol" data-paper-title="FinanceHarness: Autonomous Financial Deep Research Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-finance-harness-protocol-8c1ac9fa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bbb3ce54beabf3be">Is a FinanceGym rubric score of 3 a 3% success rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afinance-harness-protocol">FinanceHarness: Autonomous Financial Deep Research Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A rubric uses five grades from 0 through 4, and 3 is one level. Normalize within each item by its four-point maximum before averaging items. Interpretation still depends on the rubric. Raw levels, normalized item scores, and overall Outcome are distinct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For two rubrics scored 3 and 1, the item score is (3+1)/(4×2)=0.5, not 4% or a two-item hit rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27853v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27853-finance-harness-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bbb3ce54beabf3be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:finance-harness-protocol" data-paper-title="FinanceHarness: Autonomous Financial Deep Research Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ffeae55e9d1c6ba">Why keep predictions verifiable after the cutoff with the post-submission evaluator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afinance-harness-protocol">FinanceHarness: Autonomous Financial Deep Research Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Research may use only evidence available by cutoff. Earlier access to future materials turns prediction into repetition. Thesis and rubric also remain with the grader; normalize per item before averaging. Leakage invalidates the run rather than justifying dropping or zeroing a row.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Later earnings can verify a forecast after submission, but must not be backfilled into the earlier evidence pack.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27853v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27853-finance-harness-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ffeae55e9d1c6ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:finance-harness-protocol" data-paper-title="FinanceHarness: Autonomous Financial Deep Research Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a30f6f4a0d087a4a">How does equal weighting by item differ from pooling all rubrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afinance-harness-protocol">FinanceHarness: Autonomous Financial Deep Research Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Items have different counts. Pooling gives detailed items more weight; normalize per item first and then average. Do not replace the five-point rubric with an arbitrary continuous scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An item with ten criteria should not automatically weigh five times one with two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27853v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27853-finance-harness-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a30f6f4a0d087a4a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:finance-harness-protocol" data-paper-title="FinanceHarness: Autonomous Financial Deep Research Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aebea6d3c661cc2f">Can a finance-protocol row with time leakage be set to zero and included in the mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afinance-harness-protocol">FinanceHarness: Autonomous Financial Deep Research Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Invalidate the run rather than silently dropping or zeroing the row. publication_date must be no later than cutoff, and thesis, rubric, and future evidence stay away from the agent. This is a point-in-time evaluation protocol, not investment advice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool finding an article published after the cutoff is not merely one wrong answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27853v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27853-finance-harness-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aebea6d3c661cc2f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentdebugx" data-paper-title="AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agentdebugx-4b7d80dc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6920629fc1f372f">Why does AgentDebugX preserve immutable raw traces and layer diagnoses on top?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentdebugx">AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Failure analysis needs the original sequence and evidence; overwriting logs hides behavior. Detect, Attribute, Recover, and Rerun produce separately traceable artifacts. The symptom step is not necessarily the cause.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool error late in a trace may originate from bad arguments supplied earlier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与评测边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18754v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.18754-agentdebugx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6920629fc1f372f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentdebugx" data-paper-title="AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-762711639f7eb829">Why must repair proposals not automatically replay arbitrary external tools from imported logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentdebugx">AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logs are observations and can be stale, unauthorized, or side-effecting. Separate diagnosis and attribution from authorized execution. Layer hypotheses and suggestions over immutable traces, and create independent rerun evidence after a human or policy gate. Reference-privileged diagnosis is distinct from answer-free online ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A recorded command deleting a temporary folder should not run on import. Suggest a repair, then let authorized execution decide.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与评测边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18754v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.18754-agentdebugx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-762711639f7eb829">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentdebugx" data-paper-title="AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceae50a35c7df48b">What comparison boundary does the reference answer in Who&amp;When introduce?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentdebugx">AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The diagnostic receives the task answer but not the responsible agent or step, so it is localization with ground truth. Do not omit that privilege and present it as an answer-free online capability test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing the intended result helps find deviations but does not identify who first erred.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与评测边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18754v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.18754-agentdebugx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceae50a35c7df48b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentdebugx" data-paper-title="AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-68e7cd5de654ac2b">May AgentDebugX automatically replay tools from logs after proposing repairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentdebugx">AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Real reruns need a human or policy gate. Imported logs do not authorize arbitrary external commands. Score a real independent post-repair trajectory for loop evidence. Paper results did not evaluate memory or Error Hub gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a log contains a deletion, the debugger may propose a correction rather than rerunning the command.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与评测边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18754v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.18754-agentdebugx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-68e7cd5de654ac2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:logact" data-paper-title="LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-logact-bec0d56e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-db41d8cd460b9232">Why does LogAct separate vote commit from execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alogact">LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Persist intent, review, and commit before execution, separating authorization from external effects and enabling crash audit. Agreement in conversation is not a trusted durable commit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record approval before an executor calls a payment API.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07988v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.07988-logact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db41d8cd460b9232">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:logact" data-paper-title="LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-219db6899dfab0c3">Why can&#x27;t a committed action be executed again unconditionally after a crash?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alogact">LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Commit records approval but may not reveal whether the external side effect happened. A call can succeed before its receipt is logged. Recovery needs idempotency keys or transaction contracts to distinguish those cases. Votes govern approval, not external exactly-once execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If payment succeeds and the process crashes before logging a result, blind replay may charge twice. Use idempotency or transaction lookup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07988v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.07988-logact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-219db6899dfab0c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:logact" data-paper-title="LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c65844ffb886b1c4">How does LogAct k-of-N approval differ from waiting for every vote?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alogact">LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed threshold permits commit as soon as k approvals arrive. Reject early if approvals plus remaining votes cannot reach k. Irrelevant pending votes need not finish, and a voter counts once. This does not implement all dynamic approval policies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With three voters and a threshold of two, two approvals suffice. Two rejections make the last vote unable to reach two approvals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07988v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.07988-logact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c65844ffb886b1c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:logact" data-paper-title="LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b73e475fbcd5cecd">How does local LogAct handle quorum and crash recovery?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alogact">LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Require k approvals from N named voters, deduplicate voters, and disallow vote changes. Started without Result does not retry by default. Only explicit recovery for a known idempotent action, after excluding live executors, uses a stable key. Arbitrary dynamic policy languages are unsupported.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One person&#x27;s two votes do not count twice, and a commit does not justify replaying unknown side effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tfrbench" data-paper-title="TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-tfrbench-2bbb3dcd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-98893c798861ce4a">Why does TFRBench check both numerical error and reasoning consistency?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atfrbench">TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Kentucky</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A close forecast may be luck and a fluent explanation may forecast badly. References need both criteria. Labels and feedback used in construction do not yield held-out ability scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lucky trend guess without evidence and a justified forecast with large errors both fail full admission.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05364">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.05364-tfrbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98893c798861ce4a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tfrbench" data-paper-title="TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9748b5565a2ace11">Why must a summary forecast and pass independently after a long reasoning trace meets reference gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atfrbench">TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Kentucky</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summaries can omit decisive evidence and cannot inherit original correctness. Numerical accuracy and reasoning consistency jointly constrain references. Label-informed filtering measures construction quality, not held-out ability. Reject zero historical scales rather than adding arbitrary epsilon.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long trace explains seasonality and predicts correctly, while a summary saying only &#x27;upward trend&#x27; may predict badly. Check compression independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05364">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.05364-tfrbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9748b5565a2ace11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tfrbench" data-paper-title="TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da5746f15012a652">How does TFRBench MASE differ in scale from comparing raw MAE across series?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atfrbench">TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Kentucky</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MASE divides error by historical mean absolute seasonal differences, defining thresholds relative to each series. MAE retains original units and is not directly comparable across dimensions. MASE below one is a numeric gate alongside separate consistency. Zero historical scale makes it undefined.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An error of ten has different meaning for volatile sales and nearly constant temperature. Normalize by each series&#x27; historical seasonal changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05364">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.05364-tfrbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da5746f15012a652">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tfrbench" data-paper-title="TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-52b59b4d02f11ef2">Can TFRBench add epsilon and award a high score when historical seasonal scale is zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atfrbench">TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Kentucky</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MASE is undefined and the sample must be rejected. Reference admission strictly requires MASE below one and S at least four. Document composite ranking weights; local settings are not the authors&#x27; unique formula. Future truth remains with the grader.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Constant histories have no difference scale. Inventing a denominator does not make their errors comparable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05364">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.05364-tfrbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52b59b4d02f11ef2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:convapparel" data-paper-title="ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">

<span id="paper-agent-research-convapparel-e8aab87b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bed15d23c527866b">Is ConvApparel&#x27;s PLSA the topic model with the same acronym?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aconvapparel">ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Population-Level Statistical Alignment compares behavior distributions of simulated and human populations. The local kernel uses KS distance and tie-aware MWU. Group alignment does not establish human realism in every dialogue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Comparing human and simulator turn-count distributions is population alignment, not learning latent topics from shopping text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
