<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:convapparel" data-paper-title="ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd3497205b271356">Why doesn&#x27;t achieving a simulated shopping goal prove that the simulator behaves like a human?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aconvapparel">ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success measures cooperation with the current recommender. Tone, behavior distributions, and response patterns can still be unrealistic. Population statistics, trained real/fake discrimination, and cross-policy counterfactuals test distinct dimensions. HLS is the classifier&#x27;s probability of human behavior, not task success or human approval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A simulator accepting the first item immediately can succeed quickly without human-like comparison and may fail under another recommender.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.16938-convapparel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd3497205b271356">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:convapparel" data-paper-title="ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf4fa51f825f70b0">How does cross-recommender validation differ from testing under the policy used to generate simulated data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aconvapparel">ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same-policy testing may show adaptation to a familiar interaction. Cross-policy tests put a simulator trained under one recommender into another to see whether behavior transfers. This complements distribution matching and discrimination but does not guarantee every deployment policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train with a popularity-oriented recommender, then check whether shopping responses remain reasonable under an exploration-oriented one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.16938-convapparel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf4fa51f825f70b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:convapparel" data-paper-title="ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-18442e94ba96dd81">Is PLSA a topic model here, and how are local statistical choices documented?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aconvapparel">ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No; it is Population-Level Statistical Alignment. Exact permutation for small samples and fixed-seed, plus-one-corrected Monte Carlo for larger ones are explicit local choices. Train and validate the HLS classifier independently rather than filling predictions from gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A passing KS-distance calculation verifies the statistic, not human alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.16938-convapparel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18442e94ba96dd81">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-armor" data-paper-title="CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-causal-armor-73cc1cba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-94b3dc3d98d854cc">Why does CausalArmor compare user and tool attribution before privileged actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-armor">CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Untrusted tool content can dominate a proposal. Leave-one-out ablation measures likelihood changes for the same action. If tool attribution exceeds user attribution, selectively sanitize and propose again rather than executing the original action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A webpage can suggest deleting files despite no such user request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07918">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.07918-causal-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94b3dc3d98d854cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-armor" data-paper-title="CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-58882c2ee223a900">Why isn&#x27;t lower action likelihood after removing an untrusted span a causal safety proof?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-armor">CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Leave-one-out ablation shows a change in probability, but removal can change context structure or remove legitimate evidence. Compare user attribution, sanitize only flagged spans, mask contaminated continuation, and repropose. Preserve threshold direction and recomputation; low user attribution alone does not establish an attack.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a paragraph contains both a necessary number and a suspicious instruction, its likelihood effect cannot all be attributed to malicious content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07918">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.07918-causal-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58882c2ee223a900">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-armor" data-paper-title="CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f8a4f14c30948ed">How does targeted sanitation of flagged tool spans differ from deleting all tool results?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-armor">CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep unflagged evidence, sanitize flagged spans, and mask potentially contaminated assistant content after the first hit before reproposing. Deleting all tool results also removes legitimate evidence. Reevaluate the new proposal; text removal does not guarantee safety.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sanitize an injected instruction and remove affected later drafts while retaining unrelated valid retrieval evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07918">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.07918-causal-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f8a4f14c30948ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-armor" data-paper-title="CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-581064307ea1ff67">What happens when CausalArmor has no sanitizer or reproposal callback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-armor">CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Withhold the action and mark intervention_required instead of fabricating sanitation or reruns. Mask assistant content after the first hit. Larger τ flags more spans; preserve the sign and require normal authorization for any eventual action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Without a real sanitizer, deleting a string is not a successful defense loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07918">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.07918-causal-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-581064307ea1ff67">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:airs-bench" data-paper-title="AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-airs-bench-3e226cbd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d73d79eb709b84b">Is a written method suggestion enough for AIRS-Bench?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aairs-bench">AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Starting from a problem, dataset, and metric, the agent must propose a method, implement training, analyze experiments, and revise. The agent, search scaffold, and execution harness are distinct. A plausible plan is not a completed experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Suggesting a different loss is a start; implement and run it, then revise using permitted feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2602.06855-airs-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d73d79eb709b84b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:airs-bench" data-paper-title="AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7d53ec839366385">Why give AIRS-Bench problems, data, and metrics without directly providing baseline solutions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aairs-bench">AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Research involves proposals, implementation, analysis, and revision; complete solutions reduce autonomous design. Distinguish agent, search scaffold, and runtime so outer tree-search gains are not fully attributed to the model. Human SOTA is a comparison, not an answer script.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give classification data and scoring rules and let the agent design experiments. Providing the best training code would mostly test script execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:airs-bench" data-paper-title="AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-58a3a38594282860">Why match budgets when comparing sequential MLGym with tree-search AIRA-dojo?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aairs-bench">AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search design affects coverage and cost, and unrestricted branching can consume more evaluations. Fix resources and isolate labels to assess scaffold differences. Metrics from different tasks cannot simply be added.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tenfold increase in candidates can yield better models without the gain coming entirely from the search method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-b06e8ae9651a392c">Does access to an AIRS-Bench scoring script imply access to test labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aairs-bench">AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Submit predictions to isolated test scoring and use only permitted validation feedback for selection. Author results above SOTA on some tasks are not local results; full research training must actually run for a reproduction claim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing the metric is accuracy does not reveal any example&#x27;s correct class.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lifeagentbench" data-paper-title="LifeAgentBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Long-Horizon, Cross-Dimensional Lifestyle Health Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d90e5f74c4f4986f">Why do LifeAgentBench&#x27;s long-term life records require more than classifying one event?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alifeagentbench">LifeAgentBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Long-Horizon, Cross-Dimensional Lifestyle Health Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Questions span times, dimensions, or users across diet, sleep, activity, and mood records. Gather relevant evidence before calculating or comparing. Filtering and aggregation scope are part of the answer; a single record rarely suffices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>To compare activity and sleep for one user over a week, use both kinds of records for the same dates. One day&#x27;s step count is incomplete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lifeagentbench" data-paper-title="LifeAgentBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Long-Horizon, Cross-Dimensional Lifestyle Health Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d23f60fee3459ab1">Why doesn&#x27;t an SQL scorer computing definitive answers implement LifeAgent tool reasoning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alifeagentbench">LifeAgentBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Long-Horizon, Cross-Dimensional Lifestyle Health Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The scorer uses rules and records to verify final answers; it does not decompose tasks, retrieve evidence, maintain statistics, or revise plans. Keep scorer and tool baseline distinct and do not let actors read reference calculations. Field checks are not long-term health-record reasoning; this describes evaluation, not health advice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A verifier can compute mean weekly sleep, but the agent must choose the window, query records, and check missing values without calling the reference-answer function.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13880v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.13880-lifeagentbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d23f60fee3459ab1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lifeagentbench" data-paper-title="LifeAgentBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Long-Horizon, Cross-Dimensional Lifestyle Health Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5961b103e689800b">How do executable SQL, complete evidence, and final correctness differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alifeagentbench">LifeAgentBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Long-Horizon, Cross-Dimensional Lifestyle Health Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Executability concerns syntax and runtime. EX measures evidence completeness on its defined denominator, and Acc|EX checks answers given complete evidence. Mixing denominators conceals retrieval or reasoning problems.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A query can execute but omit a required user and fail to collect all evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13880v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.13880-lifeagentbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5961b103e689800b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lifeagentbench" data-paper-title="LifeAgentBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Long-Horizon, Cross-Dimensional Lifestyle Health Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7e908d939e49c24">How do read-only SQL and Context Prompting isolate gold answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alifeagentbench">LifeAgentBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Long-Horizon, Cross-Dimensional Lifestyle Health Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>For SQL, the model generates an allowed query before receiving results. Context Prompting selects public evidence by user first. Gold stays with the scorer. Numeric grading follows piecewise tolerances, and multi-item answers must match item counts, not merely substrings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct term accompanied by extra incorrect items is not a fully correct answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13880v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.13880-lifeagentbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7e908d939e49c24">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coreflect" data-paper-title="CoReflect: A Reflective Co-Evolution Framework for Improving Conversational Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-73a0fa96c34acc53">What do CoReflect&#x27;s planner, simulator, evaluator, and analyzer produce?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoreflect">CoReflect: A Reflective Co-Evolution Framework for Improving Conversational Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The planner organizes tasks, the simulator generates interactions, the evaluator applies current criteria, and the analyzer distills reflection that changes later tasks and criteria. These are semantic model roles, not four JSON fields. Local work did not substitute handwritten rules for them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An ambiguous criterion appears during dialogue. The analyzer identifies it, then later rounds revise the rubric and plan scenarios that test the issue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12208v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.12208-coreflect/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-73a0fa96c34acc53">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coreflect" data-paper-title="CoReflect: A Reflective Co-Evolution Framework for Improving Conversational Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9336a21730fbc0d6">Why can&#x27;t editing rubric strings or averaging supplied scores reproduce CoReflect&#x27;s reflective co-evolution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoreflect">CoReflect: A Reflective Co-Evolution Framework for Improving Conversational Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The core needs semantic planning of scenarios, dialogue simulation, evaluation, and an analyzer that uses reasons to identify deficits and update both tasks and criteria. Mechanical state transitions are scaffolding without semantic judgment or real interaction. Source formulas explain the loop, not local execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An analyzer should identify missed empathy criteria and create relevant scenarios. Manually changing a weight from one to two does not provide that reflection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12208v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.12208-coreflect/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9336a21730fbc0d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coreflect" data-paper-title="CoReflect: A Reflective Co-Evolution Framework for Improving Conversational Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-27514a4a3c2740e3">How does CoReflect persona–scenario consistency checking differ from valid JSON?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoreflect">CoReflect: A Reflective Co-Evolution Framework for Improving Conversational Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Syntax only makes fields readable, not semantically compatible. The paper retains pairs passing actual LLM consistency checks. This filter is part of task quality; a state machine or manual score does not replace semantic checking and reflection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A persona unable to use the internet paired with a completed online booking can be valid JSON and still require semantic review.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coreflect" data-paper-title="CoReflect: A Reflective Co-Evolution Framework for Improving Conversational Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-16d199a59b834d14">Did the local project implement CoReflect&#x27;s 953 scenarios and full semantic modules?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoreflect">CoReflect: A Reflective Co-Evolution Framework for Improving Conversational Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. This is literature coverage without a heuristic adapter. JSON state transitions or averaging supplied values do not replace LLM checks and dialogue generation; formulas explain the source method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>More loop iterations do not show the evaluator learned a new judgment dimension.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sopbench-protocol" data-paper-title="SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sopbench-protocol-97674f6a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8304d284c96dd917">Do SOPBench service constraint nodes record chat turns or define required pre-service checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asopbench-protocol">SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The graph connects services to constraints and constraints to executable helper checks, specifying permission and prerequisites rather than summarizing dialogue order. Follow each service&#x27;s dependencies to see what must be verified, not just whether final text sounds fluent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a service requires eligibility, the graph should link to that constraint and helper rather than merely contain &#x27;I checked.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08669v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2503.08669-sopbench-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8304d284c96dd917">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sopbench-protocol" data-paper-title="SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf216373788d6b3c">Why can correct final database state still fail SOPBench?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asopbench-protocol">SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The service must be permitted and required helpers executed in order. And, Or, and Chain encode distinct conditions; guessing the result cannot bypass procedure. Full success requires eligibility, state, and procedure together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A refund amount can be correct while the agent skipped order eligibility. A later check does not satisfy a chain requiring eligibility first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08669v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2503.08669-sopbench-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf216373788d6b3c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sopbench-protocol" data-paper-title="SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f5c9691726e12bb8">How do And, Or, and Chain constraints differ in verification order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asopbench-protocol">SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>And needs every condition without imposing suborder. Or allows a verified true branch. Chain enforces sequence. Treating them as unordered sets permits violations like acting before checking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identity verification before a transfer is Chain; checking after the transfer does not satisfy it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08669v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2503.08669-sopbench-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f5c9691726e12bb8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sopbench-protocol" data-paper-title="SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd44b09f931686f2">Can agent self-reports replace SOPBench helper-call records?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asopbench-protocol">SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. procedure_complete needs trusted execution traces showing actual checks in graph order. Gold stays with graders. This protocol component is not a full production service agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Saying &#x27;I verified it&#x27; is not a logged successful helper call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gaia" data-paper-title="GAIA" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-gaia-62649810" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-802c89c175ab9d3e">Does GAIA expect a long reasoning transcript or a checkable short final answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agaia">GAIA</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Score the final answer by exact comparison after prescribed normalization. Solving may still require browsing, images, and tools. Reasoning and submission format are distinct, so many plausible steps do not guarantee a match, and format failure cannot be hidden as reasoning success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a question asks for a person, submit the checkable name. Search notes without a clear final name are not automatically correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12983">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-802c89c175ab9d3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gaia" data-paper-title="GAIA" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7f1f7590b48a18a3">Why can exact short answers still test multi-tool reasoning rather than memorization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agaia">GAIA</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short output is the scoring interface; finding it can require browsing, multimodal understanding, calculation, and cross-source checks. Normalized matching makes endpoints clear, not evidence quality or failure location. Distinguish accuracy from executed traces and never put reference answers into agent prompts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One final year may require identifying a person from a picture, researching an event, and verifying dates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12983">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7f1f7590b48a18a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gaia" data-paper-title="GAIA" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9451bc182cb840df">How does normalized GAIA exact match differ from an LLM judge assigning semantic scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agaia">GAIA</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exact match checks equality after fixed normalization. A semantic judge decides equivalent meaning and has different tolerance and biases. Changing the evaluator cannot silently keep the same GAIA score. Predefine normalization instead of rewriting predictions after seeing gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One normalizer handles permitted surface variation. Asking a model to accept a vague paraphrase changes the grader.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12983">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9451bc182cb840df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gaia" data-paper-title="GAIA" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-38f78acc30af0647">May GAIA normalization be relaxed arbitrarily after inspecting gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agaia">GAIA</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fix allowed normalization and task sets, and expose gold only to the scorer. Local interface or protocol checks lack real web and multimodal runs and cannot report benchmark scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing rules because a wrong answer contains a correct substring changes the evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbench" data-paper-title="AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-autoformbench-7806e713" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1e8b44a41b19cb0">Why does AutoformBench require all proof obligations in a task to pass?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbench">AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Advanced formalization requires definitions, auxiliary lemmas, and final proof to work together. A single fragment is insufficient. Trusted Lean/Mathlib must verify all obligations; partial counts do not replace task success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A main theorem with a dependency still containing sorry is not a complete task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/autoformbench/blob/af1aa38fd44e019e566bce0b5a168609a886d8e6/paper.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/autoformbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1e8b44a41b19cb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbench" data-paper-title="AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4b095973d365cfd">Why aren&#x27;t source-present and source-free scores comparable by task ID alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbench">AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Visible materials change difficulty: a source or proof offers definitions and strategies, while a source-free workspace requires more autonomous construction. Matching task names do not align information. All obligations must pass, and failures, budget overruns, and infrastructure errors stay in the denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For the same theorem, one group reads a textbook proof while another gets only a Lean skeleton. Match source conditions before attributing score differences to the model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/autoformbench/blob/af1aa38fd44e019e566bce0b5a168609a886d8e6/paper.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/autoformbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4b095973d365cfd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbench" data-paper-title="AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9943b69a42b057f3">How does AutoformBench differ from filling one isolated Lean proof with all definitions given?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbench">AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It also requires constructing definitions and supporting lemmas, then satisfying every obligation. An isolated proof usually starts with more context fixed. Shared Lean verification does not mean equal autonomous formalization work or comparable pooled success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a definition is missing, formalize it and prove supporting lemmas. Filling only the final by block is incomplete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/autoformbench/blob/af1aa38fd44e019e566bce0b5a168609a886d8e6/paper.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/autoformbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9943b69a42b057f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbench" data-paper-title="AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c1b69021b889269">Can the AutoformBench interface drop failed, over-budget, or infrastructure-error rows?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbench">AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep the full fixed task set and actual CSV costs. Nominal caps do not imply equal spend. Importing existing verdicts is not running Harbor; mark planned runs as such if unexecuted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Counting only successfully launched tasks hides environment failures and inflates results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/autoformbench/blob/af1aa38fd44e019e566bce0b5a168609a886d8e6/paper.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/autoformbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3c1b69021b889269">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

How can we distinguish model success, a permissive environment, scorer bias, and unsafe overreach?

## Takeaway

Fix tasks, visible inputs, allowed actions, success conditions, and budget before scoring. GAIA asks real-world questions requiring tools and reasoning. Perturbation protocols change one factor and test the same goal. Safety checks also ask whether actions were justified and authorized; a correct answer does not excuse overreach. Separation of actor and scorer information is part of the protocol.

## Example

To study robustness, run one task twice, changing only an irrelevant redundant tool field with backend, data, and success condition fixed. If a necessary field is removed, the task may become impossible and cannot be counted as simple brittleness. When scoring times out, report scored outcomes and unscored counts rather than dropping unknowns.

## Common pitfall

Valid syntax does not guarantee preserved meaning, and simulator scores are not real-user or production evidence. The local GAIA mini-suite and AgentPerturb CPU interface are not complete official benchmarks. Safety fixtures do not establish attack-defense rates. Literature-only and cost-only reviews are not verified capabilities.

## Reading order

Read GAIA for end-to-end task design and difficulty, then AgentPerturb for single-factor, goal-preserving paired tests and independent verification. Distinguish official tasks, CPU protocols, and unrun parts in each local scope.

1. [GAIA](../../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12983)
2. [AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations](../../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21624)

## Check your understanding

Of 100 tasks, 80 were scored and 60 succeeded. Can we report only 75% success and omit the other 20?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Report 75% as conditional on being scored, and keep the full denominator of 100 and 20 unknowns. With equal weights, overall success lies between 60% and 80%. Attribute execution failure, interrupted scoring, and genuine task errors separately.

</details>
